# Data dictionary

<!-- Generated by docs/build_docs.py. Edits here are overwritten; the prose
     lives in docs/lineage.py and in the SQL files themselves. -->

Every table and column in the warehouse, read from `sys.columns` on Developer Edition 16.0.4265.3.

The **Source** column traces each field back to the FHIR element it came from; `docs/data-map.md` shows the same relationship the other way round, from the resource down. A test asserts the two agree with the database.

> Row counts describe the build this file was generated from — see `metrics.json` for which population that was. Everything else here is structure and does not move with the data.

## `raw`

FHIR JSON exactly as received. Never edited, never deleted.

### `norm.encounter`

**1,744 rows.**

| Column | Type | Null | Key | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `encounter_id` | `varchar(64)` | **no** | PK | `Encounter.id` | Degenerate dimension — a business key carried on the fact with no dimension table behind it. |
| `patient_id` | `varchar(64)` | **no** | FK &rarr; `norm.patient` | `Encounter.subject.reference` | Literal reference (Patient/<id>). Resolved to the patient version current at period_start, not to the version current now. |
| `status` | `varchar(20)` | **no** |  | `Encounter.status` | 1..1. Required value set. |
| `class_code` | `varchar(20)` | **no** |  | `Encounter.class.code` | 1..1, and a bare Coding rather than a CodeableConcept — there is no .coding array to descend into. |
| `class_display` | `nvarchar(100)` | yes |  | `Encounter.class.display` |  |
| `type_code_concept_id` | `int` | yes | FK &rarr; `norm.code_concept` | `Encounter.type[0].coding[0]` |  |
| `period_start` | `datetime2(3)` | yes |  | `Encounter.period.start` | Looked up in DimDate rather than computed, so a date outside the dimension degrades to Unknown instead of failing the foreign key and the whole load. |
| `period_end` | `datetime2(3)` | yes |  | `Encounter.period.end` |  |
| `service_provider_id` | `varchar(64)` | yes | FK &rarr; `norm.organization` | `Encounter.serviceProvider.reference` | CONDITIONAL reference: Organization?identifier=<system>|<value>. Resolved via norm.organization_identifier. |
| `primary_performer_id` | `varchar(64)` | yes | FK &rarr; `norm.practitioner` | `Encounter.participant[*].individual.reference` | CONDITIONAL reference on NPI. The participant whose type is PPRF is preferred; the list also holds admitters and translators. |

**Constraints**

- `CK_encounter_class` — `([class_code]='VR' OR [class_code]='SS' OR [class_code]='PRENC' OR [class_code]='OBSENC' OR [class_code]='NONAC' OR [class_code]='ACUTE' OR [class_code]='IMP' OR [class_code]='HH' OR [class_code]='FLD' OR [class_code]='EMER' OR [class_code]='AMB')`
- `CK_encounter_period` — `([period_end] IS NULL OR [period_start] IS NULL OR [period_end]>=[period_start])`
- `CK_encounter_status` — `([status]='unknown' OR [status]='entered-in-error' OR [status]='cancelled' OR [status]='finished' OR [status]='onleave' OR [status]='in-progress' OR [status]='triaged' OR [status]='arrived' OR [status]='planned')`

**Indexes**

- `IX_encounter_org` — NONCLUSTERED (service_provider_id)
- `IX_encounter_patient` — NONCLUSTERED (patient_id)
- `IX_encounter_performer` — NONCLUSTERED (primary_performer_id)
- `PK_encounter` — CLUSTERED UNIQUE (encounter_id)

### `norm.medication_request`

**1,225 rows.**

| Column | Type | Null | Key | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `medication_request_id` | `varchar(64)` | **no** | PK | `MedicationRequest.id` |  |
| `patient_id` | `varchar(64)` | **no** | FK &rarr; `norm.patient` | `MedicationRequest.subject.reference` |  |

| `intent` | `varchar(20)` | **no** |  | `MedicationRequest.intent` | 1..1. |
| `code_concept_id` | `int` | yes | FK &rarr; `norm.code_concept` | `MedicationRequest.medicationCodeableConcept.coding[0]` | medication[x] branch one. RxNorm. |
| `medication_reference_id` | `varchar(64)` | yes |  | `MedicationRequest.medicationReference.reference` | medication[x] branch two, taken by 16% of the rows in this extract. A check constraint enforces exactly one branch, which is the FHIR rule written down. |
